mechanism: Hydrochlorothiazide can cause hypokalemia and hyperglycemia, which may complicate thyroid disease management; propylthiouracil rarely causes agranulocytosis, and thiazide-induced electrolyte abnormalities may increase risk.
action: Monitor serum potassium and glucose levels regularly; consider alternative antihypertensive if electrolyte disturbances develop; ensure periodic CBC monitoring for propylthiouracil-related cytopenias.
